title: The published open coefficient square is the identity action comparison
statement:
Let $a:\Lambda\to\Lambda'$ be a map of commutative condensed rings, and let $j:U\hookrightarrow X$ be an open immersion of schemes [sk-def-sfb-coefficient-change, def-weil-open-immersion]. Put $A_T=\Lambda_T$, $B_T=\Lambda'_T$, and let $a_T:A_T\to B_T$ be the pulled-back coefficient map for $T=U,X$. Write $F=j^{-1}$ on abelian sheaves, with its strong monoidal structure $\mu$ [sk-def-sfb-transport], and write $\alpha_A:F(A_X)\xrightarrow{\sim}A_U$, $\alpha_B:F(B_X)\xrightarrow{\sim}B_U$ for the canonical coefficient isomorphisms [lem-sfb-alpha-iso]. Use the module-object pullbacks $R_A=\operatorname{Ext}_{\alpha_A}\operatorname{mapMod}(F)$ and $R_B=\operatorname{Ext}_{\alpha_B}\operatorname{mapMod}(F)$ [sk-def-sfb-module-pushforward-pullback], and scalar restrictions $r_T=\operatorname{Res}_{a_T}$ [sk-def-sfb-change-of-scalars]. Let $c^0:r_UR_B\xrightarrow{\sim}R_Ar_X$ be the specified comparison of [def-sfb-comap-upper-star-iso], formed using the invertible coefficient-square comparison [def-sfb-extend-comap-iso-of-iso].

For an ordinary $B_X$-module $N$, identify the extension along each $\alpha$ with restriction along $\alpha^{-1}$ by the balanced collapse $x\otimes n\mapsto\alpha^{-1}(x)n$, whose inverse is $n\mapsto1\otimes n$. Under these identifications, the actions on $r_UR_BN$ and $R_Ar_XN$ are both the transported $F(B_X)$-action restricted along
$$\alpha_B^{-1}a_U=F(a_X)\alpha_A^{-1}:A_U\longrightarrow F(B_X).$$
The components $c^0_N$ and $(c^0_N)^{-1}$ are the identity on the underlying sheaf $FN$, naturally in $N$; both functors send a module morphism $h$ to $Fh$ under the same identifications. Let $d^0:R_Ar_X\xrightarrow{\sim}r_UR_B$ denote this identity action comparison. On ordinary unbounded derived module categories [sk-def-sfb-derived-categories], write $R,r$ also for the corresponding levelwise functors, and let $d:R_Ar_X\xrightarrow{\sim}r_UR_B$ be the localization of $d^0$ degreewise. Then the specified derived comparison $c$ of [def-sfb-derived-comap-upper-star-iso] satisfies $c^{-1}=d$, as a natural isomorphism of derived functors. No flatness of $a$ is assumed.

proof.text: Work in $\mathcal C_T=\Sh(T_{\mathrm{proét}},\Ab)$, $T=X,U$. By the existing sheaf-category instances of [lem-weil-pbc-sheaf-tensor-closed], these are abelian symmetric monoidal closed categories with equalizers and coequalizers, additive tensor product, and tensor preserving colimits in each variable. Thus the hypotheses of [lem-sfb-extension-iso-quotient-formula] hold for the commutative coefficient ring isomorphisms $\alpha_A,\alpha_B$ of [lem-sfb-alpha-iso]. Apply that lemma to an arbitrary module $M$ over $F(A_X)$ or $F(B_X)$, respectively. Denote its specified collapse by $p_{A,M}$ or $p_{B,M}$, and its inverse by $s_{A,M}$ or $s_{B,M}$. The lemma gives $p_{A,M}(x\otimes m)=\alpha_A^{-1}(x)m$ and $s_{A,M}(m)=1\otimes m$, and the analogous $B$-formulas, as identities of internal sheaf morphisms through the balancing coequalizer. They are natural module isomorphisms, so they identify the actual extension-along-isomorphism comparisons, not just the isomorphism classes of the extended modules.

source.place: First sentence, normalized by the existing quotient-formula lemma; its source is def-sfb-module-open-lower-shriek-adjunction.proof.md, final sentence.

proof.text:
Specialize [lem-sfb-coefficient-pullback-square] to $f=j$, source scheme $U$, target scheme $X$. It gives $\alpha_B\circ F(a_X)=a_U\circ\alpha_A$. Precompose with $\alpha_A^{-1}$ and postcompose with $\alpha_B^{-1}$, which exist by [lem-sfb-alpha-iso]. Cancellation gives
$$h:\quad\alpha_B^{-1}\circ a_U=F(a_X)\circ\alpha_A^{-1}:A_U\longrightarrow F(B_X).$$
Only the two $\alpha$ maps are inverted; $a_X$ and $a_U$ need not be invertible or flat.

source.place: Coefficient-square equality, rearranged by the two inverse identities.

proof.text:
For $N\in\Mod_{B_X}$ write $\gamma_N:B_X\otimes N\to N$ for its action. The transport and restriction formulas of [sk-def-sfb-transport] and [def-sfb-modobj-restriction], functoriality of $F$, and naturality of its monoidal structure give
$$F(\gamma_N\circ(a_X\otimes1_N))\circ\mu_{A_X,N}
=F\gamma_N\circ\mu_{B_X,N}\circ(F(a_X)\otimes1_{FN}).$$
Consequently the comparison
$$\tau_N:\operatorname{mapMod}(F)(r_XN)\xrightarrow{\sim}\operatorname{Res}_{F(a_X)}\operatorname{mapMod}(F)(N)$$
is the identity of $FN$ in both directions. Both sides send a module morphism $v$ to $Fv$, so naturality is $Fv\circ1=1\circ Fv$. This computes the transport/restriction factor used in the prescribed upper-star comparison.

source.place: Transport commutes with restriction of scalars: expand the two actions and use naturality of the monoidal structure.

proof.text:
Put $M_B=\operatorname{mapMod}(F)(N)$, $M_A=\operatorname{mapMod}(F)(r_XN)$ and $\delta_N=F\gamma_N\circ\mu_{B_X,N}$. By the module-pullback definition [sk-def-sfb-module-pushforward-pullback], the collapses of step 1 identify $r_UR_BN$ with $FN$ having action
$$\delta_N\circ((\alpha_B^{-1}\circ a_U)\otimes1),$$
and $R_Ar_XN$ with $FN$ having action
$$\delta_N\circ((F(a_X)\circ\alpha_A^{-1})\otimes1),$$
using the action calculation of step 3. Equality $h$ from step 2 identifies these actions. By [det-def-sfb-module-objects-definition], the identity of $FN$ is therefore a module isomorphism in either direction. Naturality of the collapses and the formulas for transport and restriction show that both functors act on $v$ by $Fv$ under these identifications. This gives precisely the natural identity-action comparison $d^0:R_Ar_X\xrightarrow{\sim}r_UR_B$.

source.place: Both composite actions after inverse-coefficient restriction; compare using the inverse square.

proof.text:
Compute the particular scalar-square construction named in the statement, [def-sfb-extend-comap-iso-of-iso], with $R=F(A_X)$, $S=F(B_X)$, $R'=A_U$, $S'=B_U$, $\varphi=F(a_X)$, $\psi=a_U$, and vertical maps $\alpha_A,\alpha_B$. Its prescribed composite first applies $\operatorname{Res}_{a_U}(p_{B,M_B})$, identifies the two composite restrictions along $\alpha_B^{-1}a_U=F(a_X)\alpha_A^{-1}$, and then applies $p_{A,\operatorname{Res}_{F(a_X)}M_B}^{-1}$. The middle identification has underlying identity: expanding restriction twice gives the action $\delta_N\circ(h\otimes1)$ on either side, and all restriction functors keep underlying arrows, by [def-sfb-modobj-restriction]. Hence, if $\sigma_N$ denotes this scalar-square component, cancellation of the last collapse with its inverse gives
$$p_{A,\operatorname{Res}_{F(a_X)}M_B}\circ\sigma_N=p_{B,M_B}$$
on underlying sheaves. Here the two extension comparisons $e_b,e_a$ of the scalar-square construction are, by its construction, those of clause 5 of [sk-def-sfb-change-of-scalars], and that clause takes them from [def-sfb-modobj-extension-along-iso]: they are the adjoint-uniqueness comparisons $\operatorname{Ext}_{\alpha}\cong\operatorname{Res}_{\alpha^{-1}}$. By [lem-sfb-extension-iso-quotient-formula] these comparisons are exactly the collapses $p_B=e_b$ and $p_A=e_a$ of step 1, so the composite just described is the specified one. This is a computation of the specified composite, rather than an inference that an arbitrary scalar-square isomorphism has identity components.

source.place: Entire inverse-restriction construction; explicitly the composite in WeilConjectures/CategoryTheory/ModuleObjects/ChangeOfScalarsSquare.lean, extendScalarsComapIsoOfIsIso, lines 120–129.

proof.text:
Unfold the prescribed composite of [def-sfb-comap-upper-star-iso]: after $\sigma_N$ it applies $\operatorname{Ext}_{\alpha_A}(\tau_N^{-1})$. Naturality of the collapse in [lem-sfb-extension-iso-quotient-formula] gives
$$p_{A,M_A}\circ\operatorname{Ext}_{\alpha_A}(\tau_N^{-1})
=\tau_N^{-1}\circ p_{A,\operatorname{Res}_{F(a_X)}M_B}$$
on underlying sheaves. Compose with $\sigma_N$ and use step 5 and the identity underlying $\tau_N^{-1}$ from step 3 to get $p_{A,M_A}\circ c^0_N=p_{B,M_B}$. Thus
$$p_{A,M_A}\circ c^0_N\circ p_{B,M_B}^{-1}=1_{FN},\qquad
p_{B,M_B}\circ(c^0_N)^{-1}\circ p_{A,M_A}^{-1}=1_{FN}.$$
The second equation follows by taking the inverse of the first. The faithful forgetful functor in [det-def-sfb-module-objects-definition] makes these equalities equalities of the compared module morphisms. Together with step 4 they prove $(c^0)^{-1}=d^0$ naturally, including both component directions and the action on module morphisms. In Lean expand the specified composite with local names for the two collapse isomorphisms and the transport/restriction comparison. Apply naturality of extendScalarsIsoComapInv separately to the hom and inverse components of mapModComapIso, whose underlying maps are identities. Cancel the two collapse inverse pairs in each direction. Faithfulness and cancellation then identify the ordinary natural isomorphisms.

source.place: Final displayed composite, with its transport factor and collapse factors retained; upstream ChangeOfCoefficients.lean, comapUpperStarIso, lines 177–187.

proof.text: The existing instances upperStar_additive, preservesFiniteLimits_upperStar and preservesFiniteColimits_upperStar in the module-pullback construction [sk-def-sfb-module-pushforward-pullback] already supply exactness of both actual pullbacks. Left exactness is transported along the extension-to-inverse-restriction comparison [def-sfb-modobj-extension-along-iso]; right exactness follows from the pullback adjunction. Scalar restrictions are additive and exact by [sk-def-sfb-change-of-scalars]. Consequently the levelwise derived functors and their composition factorizations exist by [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-factorization]. No separate application of the aggregate module_pullback_additive_exact theorem, flatness, boundedness or K-flat resolution is needed.

source.place: First sentence: exactness and levelwise derived extension; Stacks derived.tex Tag 015F, lemma-right-derived-exact-functor.

proof.text: Write $P=r_UR_B$ and $T=R_Ar_X$ at the abelian level. For any cochain complex $K$ of $B_X$-modules the degree-$n$ maps $c^0_{K^n}$ define a chain isomorphism $C(P)K\to C(T)K$: naturality for $d_K^n$ gives $T(d_K^n)c^0_{K^n}=c^0_{K^{n+1}}P(d_K^n)$. The maps $d^0_{K^n}$ satisfy the reverse equation. Naturality for each component of a chain map gives naturality on complexes. By step 6 the two chain isomorphisms are inverses degree by degree, so $C(c^0)^{-1}=C(d^0)$ as natural isomorphisms of functors on complexes. This also accounts for differentials: under the collapses both are $F(d_K^n)$, since step 4 applies to every module morphism.

source.place: Second sentence: spell out the levelwise natural isomorphisms and inverse chain maps.

proof.text:
Let $Q_X:C(\Mod_{B_X})\to D(\Mod_{B_X})$ and $Q_U:C(\Mod_{A_U})\to D(\Mod_{A_U})$ be localization at quasi-isomorphisms. Set $P_D=D(r_U)D(R_B)$ and $T_D=D(R_A)D(r_X)$. Composing the factorization isomorphisms of [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-factorization] gives $\phi_P:P_DQ_X\xrightarrow{\sim}Q_UC(P)$ and $\phi_T:T_DQ_X\xrightarrow{\sim}Q_UC(T)$. The construction of [def-sfb-derived-comap-upper-star-iso] localizes $C(c^0)$ using these composite factorizations. Consequently
$$c_{Q_XK}=\phi_{T,K}^{-1}Q_U(C(c^0)_K)\phi_{P,K},\qquad
d_{Q_XK}=\phi_{P,K}^{-1}Q_U(C(d^0)_K)\phi_{T,K}.$$
Step 8 makes the latter expression the inverse of the former. Clause (3) of [lem-weil-pbc-localization-universal-property] now gives $c^{-1}=d$ as natural transformations, hence as natural isomorphisms of the derived functors. Clause (2) of that node ensures that localization respects inverses and composition, including the factorization isomorphisms. This proves the stated equality on the whole unbounded category, rather than merely on a selected class of representatives. The existing proved library lemma Functor.mapDerivedCategoryNatIso_symm implements preservation of inverses using localization full faithfulness and preservation of composition. Apply it to the ordinary comparison equality from step 6 and expand the published composition factorization isomorphisms; associativity gives the required equality of natural isomorphisms.

source.place: Second sentence: descent with composite factorization isomorphisms; Stacks categories.tex Tag 04VG, lemma-properties-left-localization, and the natural-transformation full faithfulness stated in the cited Mathlib leaf.

tool_uses.why: Ambient sheaf category is Grothendieck abelian with additive tensor and all required colimits; this generic sheaf theorem verifies hypotheses of the existing internal collapse theorem without changing the coefficient-comparison route.

The normalized component formula for extension along a ring-object isomorphism fixes the actual comparisons used in the published scalar square; coefficient-comparison existence statements alone do not provide this normalization.

The exactness theorem for the actual coefficient module pullback supplies the levelwise functors; this is a property of the already fixed pullback construction, not an alternative route to a scalar comparison.
